subject: Executive escalation: MFN carve-out + benchmark cap for pilot program
messages:
From: Eve Lawrence <eve.lawrence@clearsight.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Sato <tom.sato@clearsight.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot terms + MFN/benchmark ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed. We're ready to move forward with a 6-week pilot (up to 10k API calls/day) but have two commercial asks before we sign: an MFN-style carve-out for models we co-develop during the pilot, and a benchmark cap that limits discounts tied to accuracy metrics during the pilot period.

Specifically: 1) If ClearSight invests in joint model work, we want assurance Redwood will not give our co-developed model to a direct competitor at a lower price (carve-out MFN). 2) For the pilot, we want to cap discounting tied to a benchmark metric so that any future benchmark-triggered discounts are capped at 20% for the first 12 months post-pilot.

We understand these are non-standard; we can sign a separate limited carve-out amendment for the pilot if needed. Attached is the proposed SOW and a short summary of our legal team's requested language.

Attachments: Clearsight_Pilot_SOW.pdf

Appreciate your help — happy to jump on a call to walk through.

Best,
Eve Lawrence
Head of Product, ClearSight Analytics
E: eve.lawrence@clearsight.ai
T: +1 415 555 0192

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: EXEC ESCALATION: ClearSight pilot — MFN carve-out + benchmark cap (deal DL-2026-0883)

Team — escalating for exec review. Summary below with attachments (exec_escalation_summary.pdf). Please reply with decision or requested edits.

External ask (from ClearSight):
- MFN-style carve-out limited to models co-developed during the pilot (time-boxed to pilot + 12 months).
- Benchmark-based discount cap: discounts tied to benchmark accuracy/performance will be capped at 20% for 12 months post-pilot.
- No region exclusivity requested in writing yet; Karthik asked for competitor list.

Commercial impact / risk:
- MFN carve-out sets precedent; if too broad it could restrict pricing flexibility for competitive accounts.
- Benchmark cap reduces our ability to tier discounts for performance-based guarantees — potential revenue erosion if we accept broad language.
- Pilot is 6 weeks, expected ARR conversion low-mid six figures if full expansion.

Attachments: exec_escalation_summary.pdf, redwood_discount_matrix.xlsx

Recommended options for exec:
A) Approve a narrow carve-out (explicit definition of co-developed work, list of competitor carve-outs, 12-month sunset) + reject benchmark cap — offer alternate: performance credit tied to specific evals (non-stacking) up to 10%.
B) Approve both asks conditionally: carve-out with strict limits + benchmark cap at 10% (not 20%) and internal approval from RevOps + Legal; require pilot to include pre-defined evaluation harness.
C) Reject both; offer expanded pilot at standard commercial terms or a limited trial with additional professional services to reduce model risk.

Decision needed: Marissa — pricing approval; Laura — legal redline language; Rishi — executive sign-off / commercial exceptions.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachment: exec_escalation_summary.pdf (one-page digest)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EXEC ESCALATION: ClearSight pilot — MFN carve-out + benchmark cap (deal DL-2026-0883)

Karthik / Marissa — I reviewed their proposed language. I can draft a narrow amendment that meets option A with these guardrails:
1) Define "co-developed model" as models where both parties materially contribute IP and code, and where contribution is documented in a joint development log during the pilot.
2) Carve-out applies only to commercial distribution to named competitor list (they must provide list and get prior written consent for any change).
3) Sunset the carve-out at 12 months post-pilot; include mutual right to extend only by written amendment.
4) Benchmark cap: propose alternative — a performance credit of up to 10% applied only to pilot invoices, non-recurring, and explicitly non-transferable.

If Exec approves a conditional exception to standard MFN language, Legal needs the competitor list and a robust definition of joint IP to avoid open-ended obligations. I recommend option A with the 10% performance credit rather than a 20% cap.

I can prepare the amendment language today if you confirm option A.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
